History.title: Built from real agricultural practice
History.paragraph1: The origin of Paltech lies in a family-run dairy farm. In 2016, the grandparents converted the farm to organic agriculture—an important step toward greater sustainability and responsibility toward nature and animals. However, the transition also brought new challenges: problematic weeds such as dock and ragwort began to spread increasingly. Controlling them is particularly demanding in organic farming and requires a great deal of manual labor.

paragraph2.part1: Despite all the advances in agriculture, this specific task is still largely done by hand. Dock and ragwort are removed manually—labor-intensive, time-consuming, and physically demanding. It quickly became clear: a better solution was needed.
paragraph2.part2: Since 2021, Felix, Florian, and their stepfather Jorge have been working together on this vision: the full automation of weed control in organic grassland. What began as a family problem is now the driving force behind Paltech—with the goal of sustainably relieving farmers and making agriculture more efficient.

Team.title: Developed by an interdisciplinary team
Team.description1: We are an international team with a strong Latin American influence, working passionately on forward-looking solutions for agriculture.
Team.description2: Our mix of software developers, electrical engineers, and mechanical engineers combines technical expertise with a spirit of innovation, creating a unique dynamic.

Nuga.title: European Innovation Partnership (EIP-Agri)
Nuga.description1: The European Innovation Partnership for Agricultural Productivity and Sustainability (EIP-Agri) is an EU funding instrument. Its goal is to strengthen innovation in the agricultural sector. It supports practice-oriented projects that make agriculture and food production more productive while also more sustainable.
Nuga.description2: Our NUGA project is financially supported under EIP-Agri by the European Union and the Free State of Bavaria and has a duration of 24 months.

ziel.title: Project Goal
ziel.description: The goal of the NUGA project is the development of an innovative tractor-mounted implement that enables mechanical—and therefore herbicide-free—control of dock and ragwort in grassland, thereby improving feed quality.

problem.title: Why dock and ragwort are a problem
problem.description: Dock is considered a space competitor: it displaces valuable forage plants, develops deep taproots, and produces a large number of long-lasting seeds. Mechanical removal is difficult.
problem.description2: Ragwort is toxic to animals, especially cattle and horses. Its toxicity remains even in hay.
problem.description3: In organic farming, chemical agents are not allowed—leaving manual removal as the only option. This takes about one minute per plant—an immense time effort that is hardly manageable in times of labor shortages.

results.title: Current Results
items: A digital twin of the implement has been created.
Various methods for optimizing deployment planning have been tested.
The risk analysis has been successfully completed.
The physical implementation of the implement is now beginning—a crucial step toward practical application.

hero.title: NeoBot – (Semi-)autonomous control of invasive plants
hero.description: Development of an all-terrain robot for the mechanical, herbicide-free control of invasive plant species – safe, practical, and environmentally friendly.

funding.description: A project funded under the CAP Strategic Plan Germany 2023–2027 in the Free State of Bavaria. Supported by the European Innovation Partnership (EIP-Agri).

projectGoal.title: Project Goal
projectGoal.description: Invasive plant species such as giant hogweed pose an increasing challenge for agriculture, the environment, and public safety. They displace native species, are difficult to access, and can cause health damage upon contact.
projectGoal.description2: The goal of the NeoBot project is to develop an all-terrain robot that removes these plants mechanically and without the use of herbicides. The focus is on a practical, safe, and environmentally friendly solution.
projectGoal.caption: Giant hogweed can cause severe burns

situation.title: Initial Situation
situation.description: The control of invasive neophytes is currently carried out mainly:
items: Manually (labor-intensive and risky)
Chemically (environmentally critical)
Or with equipment that is difficult to deploy
situation.description2: Especially in hard-to-reach terrain – e.g., slopes, forest edges, or near water bodies – existing solutions are only of limited use.
situation.highlight: This is where the NeoBot project comes in.

solution.title: Approach
solution.description: Within the project, an innovative system is being developed that combines the following features:
items: Operation in rough terrain
Mechanical, herbicide-free control
Combination of manual and semi-autonomous control
Intelligent detection of relevant plants
solution.description2: The system is modular and can potentially be adapted for additional applications in the future.
solution.imageAlt: Protective clothing for controlling giant hogweed
solution.caption: When removing giant hogweed, wearing protective clothing is mandatory. Otherwise, skin burns may occur.

results.title: Expected Results
results.description: The project aims to develop a functional demonstrator that can be used under real conditions.
results.description2: In particular, the following outcomes are expected:
items: A significant reduction in manual labor effort
Improved occupational safety
An environmentally friendly alternative to chemical methods
New approaches for applying modern technologies in landscape management
results.description3: In the long term, the solution aims to promote biodiversity and open new perspectives for the practical use of automated systems.

activities.title: Project Activities
activities.description: The project includes several coordinated work steps:
items: Development and integration of key system components
Adaptation to different operating conditions
Establishment of safe and reliable operation
Conducting laboratory and field tests
Accompanying communication and knowledge transfer
activities.description2: A special focus is placed on practical testing under real conditions.

milestones.title: Milestones
milestones.description: These steps form the foundation for potential future real-world application.

hero.title: Control of durchwuchskartoffeln
hero.description: Development of a robotic system for the targeted detection and mechanical removal of durchwuchskartoffeln – without the use of chemical plant protection products.

funding.description: A project funded under the CAP Strategic Plan Germany 2023–2027 in the Free State of Bavaria. Supported by the European Innovation Partnership (EIP-Agri).

projectGoal.title: Project Goal
projectGoal.description: Durchwuchskartoffeln appear as unwanted plants in subsequent crops and represent a growing challenge in arable farming. They compete with crops for resources and can promote the spread of diseases and pests.
projectGoal.description2: The aim of the project is to develop a robotic system that detects these plants in a targeted way and removes them mechanically – without the use of chemical plant protection products.
projectGoal.caption: Durchwuchskartoffeln in a maize crop

situation.title: Initial Situation
situation.description: After potato harvesting, tubers often remain in the soil and sprout again in the following years. These so-called volunteer potatoes:
items: Reduce yields in subsequent crops
Complicate crop rotations
Increase phytosanitary risks
Are difficult to fully control
situation.description2: Existing methods often focus on above-ground plant parts and insufficiently reach the tubers located in the soil.

solution.title: Approach
solution.description: Within the project, an innovative system is being developed that is specifically designed for sustainable control in the soil:
items: AI-based detection of individual plants
Precise positioning of a mechanical tool
Targeted intervention in the soil to damage the tubers
Combination of automated and supervised control
solution.description2: The focus is on interrupting the growth cycle as completely as possible by treating the mother tubers in the soil.

results.title: Expected Results
results.description: The goal is to develop a practical system that can be used under real conditions.
results.description2: In particular, the following outcomes are expected:
items: A significant reduction in the use of herbicides
More effective control through intervention in the soil
Improved field hygiene and plant health
Relief for agricultural operations
results.description3: The system is intended to be usable in both conventional and organic farming and to open new possibilities for sustainable production systems.

activities.title: Project Activities
activities.description: The project includes several key development steps:
items: Development of an AI system for plant detection
Development of mechanical tools for tuber treatment
Design of an all-terrain carrier vehicle
Integration of control and safety functions
Execution of extensive field tests
activities.description2: A special focus is placed on the combination of digitalization and mechanical processing.

hero.title: Autonomous robotics to promote biodiversity in roadside green areas
hero.description: Development of an autonomous robotic system for the ecological enhancement and efficient maintenance of roadside areas.

funding.description: Funded under the Digital GreenTech initiative – environmental technology meets robotics – by the Federal Ministry for Research, Technology and Space (BMFTR).

projectGoal.title: Project Goal
projectGoal.description: Roadside areas offer great, yet largely untapped potential for nature conservation and climate protection. The goal of the project is to develop an autonomous robotic system that enhances these areas ecologically while maintaining them efficiently.
items: Navigate roadside areas autonomously
Mow selectively and in an insect-friendly manner
Specifically suppress invasive plant species
Actively introduce native plant species
projectGoal.description3: In this way, roadside areas are actively developed into ecological corridors.

situation.title: Initial Situation
situation.description: Roadside areas are currently maintained mostly using conventional methods – often through mulching or simple mowing. This leads to several problems:
items: Promotion of competitive plant species due to nutrient accumulation
Displacement of native species
Strong spread of invasive plants (e.g., goldenrod, knotweed)
High damage to insects due to unsuitable mowing techniques
situation.description2: At the same time, large areas remain ecologically underutilized, even though they could play an important role as connectivity corridors for biodiversity.

solution.title: Approach
solution.description: The project follows an integrated, technology-based approach:
items: Autonomous navigation along roadside areas
AI-based plant and environment detection
Selective, section-based mowing instead of full-area processing
Targeted control of invasive species
Active reseeding of native plant species
solution.description2: The robot combines maintenance, monitoring, and ecological enhancement in a single system.

funding.description: Funded under the KMU-innovativ – Bioeconomy initiative by the Federal Ministry for Research, Technology and Space.

projectGoal.title: Project Goal
projectGoal.description: The goal of the Arbot project is to develop an autonomous planting robot that supports reforestation and the transition toward climate-resilient mixed forests.
items: Automatically plant seedlings
Navigate autonomously in forest environments
Operate under real-world conditions
Significantly reduce labor effort in forestry
projectGoal.description3: This addresses a key bottleneck in reforestation: the acute labor shortage.

situation.title: Initial Situation
items: Climate change-related damage (drought, bark beetles)
Increasing need for reforestation
Large-scale area requirements (hundreds of thousands of hectares)
At the same time, declining availability of labor
situation.description2: Manual planting is time-consuming, physically demanding, and difficult to scale.

items: Autonomous navigation in forests (even without GPS)
Detection of suitable planting positions
Precise planting of seedlings
Robust mobility in unstructured terrain

FAQ.title: Frequently asked questions
FAQ.description: Answers to common questions about the product, its operation, and how to get in touch with the team.

1.question: Which weeds are targeted?
1.answer: Currently, the focus is on dock (Ampfer). The next steps include autumn crocus (Herbstzeitlose) and ragwort (Kreuzkraut).

2.question: How are the weeds controlled?
2.answer: The robot automatically detects the weeds, precisely positions itself above them, and selectively mills out the root. During this process, the regrowth buds are crushed in such a way that regrowth is no longer possible. Afterwards, the resulting gap is immediately reseeded with grass. The entire process is 100% mechanical and completely avoids the use of herbicides.

3.question: How long is the robot’s battery life?
3.answer: Currently, the battery life is approximately 10 to 12 hours, depending on the operating conditions.

4.question: What is the BaySL Digital funding program about?
4.answer: The Paltech robot is listed on the BaySL Digital positive list, which allows the purchase to be subsidized by up to 40%. The application process is simple and can be completed in just a few clicks via the iBALIS portal.

5.question: Can the robot be seen on-site?
5.answer: Yes, we regularly conduct live demonstrations. You can find the upcoming dates here.

FAQ.more2: Then write to us - we will help you further!
